info.name: ShopVerse API
info.description:
Complete API collection for ShopVerse Spring Boot application.

## Setup
1. Set `baseUrl` variable to `http://localhost:8080` (already default)
2. Run **Login** or **Register** — token is captured automatically
3. All protected requests use `{{token}}` automatically

## Seed Data Flow
1. 🔐 Register Admin → set ROLE in DB (see note)
2. 🔐 Login as Admin
3. 🌱 Run all Seed: Create Product requests
4. 🔐 Register Regular User
5. 🔐 Login as User
6. 🌱 Run Seed: Place Order

request.description:
Register a new customer. Token is auto-saved to {{token}}.

**Note on ADMIN role:** After registering, update the customer's role in the DB:
```sql
UPDATE customers SET tier = 'PLATINUM' WHERE email = 'admin@shopverse.com';
```
For admin JWT role, check the AuthController registration logic — role may need to be set via direct DB or a separate admin bootstrap endpoint.

Register admin user. After this, run the following SQL to grant ADMIN role so that Create Product works:

```sql
-- Connect to shopverse DB and run:
UPDATE customers SET tier = 'PLATINUM' WHERE email = 'admin@shopverse.com';
```

Then check AuthController to confirm how 'role' is embedded in the JWT (look for role assignment in RegisterRequest handler).

request.description:
Fetches a single product by ID via @Cacheable.

**Redis flow:**
- 1st call → cache MISS → hits PostgreSQL → stores in Redis as `products::<id>` with 30 min TTL
- 2nd call → cache HIT → served from Redis, no DB call

Verify in Redis:
```
docker exec -it <redis> redis-cli
KEYS products::*
GET products::<id>
TTL products::<id>
```

Category filter uses @Cacheable via CachedProductService.findByCategory().

**Redis flow:**
- 1st call → cache MISS → hits PostgreSQL → stores in Redis as `products::category:electronics` with 30 min TTL
- 2nd call → cache HIT → served from Redis

Verify: `KEYS products::*` in redis-cli

exec: console.log('  @CacheEvict allEntries → all page/category caches cleared');
console.log('  Next GET /api/products will be a cache MISS (fresh from DB)');

request.description:
Updates product by ID. Requires ADMIN role.

**Redis flow on update:**
1. @CachePut → writes updated product to `products::<id>` (fresh individual cache)
2. @CacheEvict allEntries → clears ALL products::* keys (page caches, category caches)
3. Next GET /api/products → cache MISS → hits PostgreSQL → repopulates cache

This prevents stale page results after an update.
Deletes a product by ID. Also removes it from Elasticsearch. Requires ADMIN role. Uses {{productId}} saved from Create Product.

item.name: 🔴 Redis Inspection
item.description:
Verify Redis cache state via the ShopVerse API. Run these before and after product operations to observe cache MISS → HIT behaviour.

For direct Redis inspection use redis-cli:
  docker exec -it <redis-container> redis-cli
  KEYS *
  GET products::42
  TTL products::42

exec: console.log('👉 Redis key written: products::' + body.data.id + ' (TTL 30 min)');
console.log('👉 Now run Step 2 — first call will be a cache MISS');
console.log('👉 Then run Step 2 again — second call will be a cache HIT');

request.description:
Creates product via CreateProductUseCase → cachedProductService.save() → @CachePut

What happens in Redis:
  SET products::<id> <json> EX 1800

Verify immediately after:
  redis-cli> KEYS products::*
  redis-cli> GET products::<id>

item.name: Step 2 — Get Product by ID (1st call = MISS, 2nd call = HIT)

exec: console.log('👉 1st run: cache MISS → hit PostgreSQL → stored in Redis');
console.log('👉 2nd run: cache HIT → served from Redis, no DB call');

request.description:
GET by ID → CachedProductService.findById() → @Cacheable

1st call:
  Redis GET products::<id> → null (MISS)
  PostgreSQL SELECT WHERE id = ?
  Redis SET products::<id> <json> EX 1800

2nd call:
  Redis GET products::<id> → <json> (HIT)
  Returns immediately, PostgreSQL never called

Verify TTL counting down:
  redis-cli> TTL products::<id>

item.name: Step 3 — Get by Category (1st call = MISS, 2nd call = HIT)

exec: console.log('👉 Run again — 2nd call served from Redis');

Delete → DeleteProductUseCase → cachedProductService.evict() → @CacheEvict

item.name: 🔎 Elasticsearch Direct
item.description: Direct queries to Elasticsearch at localhost:9200 — no auth required. Use these to inspect what is indexed in ES independently of the ShopVerse API.

request.description: Check if Elasticsearch is running. Returns cluster name, version, and status.
Lists all ES indices with document count, size, and health status. Should show 'products' index after app startup.
Returns all documents in the products index (up to 10 by default). Shows raw ES document structure including _id, _source, and metadata.
Returns the total number of documents indexed in ES. Compare with PostgreSQL count to verify sync.
Fetch a specific product document from ES by ID. Uses {{productId}} saved from Create Product. Returns 404 if not yet indexed.
Full-text match query on product name. Change 'MacBook' to any keyword. Returns score-ranked results.
Exact term match on category field. Use 'term' (not 'match') for exact keyword fields. Change 'electronics' to any category.
Searches across name, description, and category fields simultaneously with fuzzy matching. This is what ShopVerse's /api/search endpoint uses internally.
Filter products by price range. Change gte (greater than or equal) and lte (less than or equal) values as needed.
Shows the field mappings for the products index — field types, analyzers, whether fields are indexed. Useful for debugging search issues.
Returns cluster health: green (all good), yellow (replicas unassigned — normal for single-node dev), red (data missing). Single-node Docker setup will always be yellow.

item.name: ⭐ Reviews (MongoDB)
item.description:
Product reviews stored in MongoDB.

**Flow:**
1. Login as User (Auth → Login)
2. Create a product (Seed Data → Create Product — Laptop)
3. Submit Review — writes to MongoDB 'reviews' collection
4. Get Reviews — reads from MongoDB
5. Get Rating Stats — runs MongoDB aggregation pipeline

Verify in MongoDB:
  docker exec -it <mongo-container> mongosh shopverse
  db.reviews.find().pretty()
  db.reviews.countDocuments()

exec: console.log('✅ Review saved to MongoDB, id:', body.data.id);

body.raw:
{
  "customerId": {{customerId}},
  "rating": 5,
  "title": "Absolutely love this product!",
  "body": "I have been using this for a month and it exceeded all my expectations. Build quality is excellent and performance is top-notch. Highly recommended for anyone looking for reliability.",
  "tags": ["excellent", "value-for-money", "highly-recommended"],
  "verified": true
}

item.name: 🗃️ Order Activity (Cassandra)
item.description:
Order activity events stored in Cassandra.

Each time an order is placed, a ORDER_PLACED event is automatically written to the Cassandra 'order_activity' table.

**Flow:**
1. Login as User → place an order → activity is logged automatically
2. GET activity to read events from Cassandra

Verify in Cassandra:
  docker exec -it <cassandra-container> cqlsh
  USE shopverse;
  SELECT * FROM order_activity;

exec: console.log('👉 Cassandra: ORDER_PLACED event written to order_activity table');
console.log('👉 Now run Get Order Activity to read from Cassandra');

request.description:
Places an order. After the PostgreSQL commit, PlaceOrderUseCase writes an ORDER_PLACED event to Cassandra:

```
INSERT INTO order_activity (customer_id, event_time, event_id, order_id, event_type, details)
VALUES ({{customerId}}, now(), uuid(), {{orderId}}, 'ORDER_PLACED', 'Order #X placed...')
```

The Cassandra write is wrapped in try-catch — if Cassandra is down the order still succeeds.

request.description: Place a second order to build activity history. After this, Get Order Activity should return 2 events for the customer, newest first.

item.name: Get All Order Activity (reads from Cassandra)

exec: console.log('✅ Activity events from Cassandra:', body.data.length);
console.warn('⚠️ No events found — place an order first');

request.description:
Reads all order activity events for the customer from Cassandra, newest first.

Cassandra query: SELECT * FROM order_activity WHERE customer_id = {{customerId}} ORDER BY event_time DESC

Partition key is customer_id — all events for a customer are on one Cassandra node. Very fast reads.

Expected after 2 orders: 2 ORDER_PLACED events, newest first.

exec: console.log('✅ Recent activity events (last hour):', body.data.length);

query.description: ISO-8601 timestamp. Returns last 50 events after this time. Change to 1 hour ago to see recent orders only.

request.description:
Returns last 50 activity events after the given timestamp.

Cassandra CQL: SELECT * FROM order_activity WHERE customer_id = ? AND event_time > ? LIMIT 50

Change the since parameter to filter by time window. Example values:
- 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z — all events this year
- 2026-06-11T00:00:00Z — all events today

item.name: Get Activity — No Orders Yet (expect empty list)

exec: console.log('✅ Empty list returned — customer 99999 has no activity');

request.description: Customer 99999 has no orders. Cassandra returns an empty result set — not a 404. This confirms the query runs successfully against Cassandra even with no matching rows.
Transitions order from PENDING to CONFIRMED. Logs ORDER_CONFIRMED event to Cassandra. Admin only.
Transitions order from CONFIRMED to PROCESSING. Logs ORDER_PROCESSING event to Cassandra. Admin only.
Transitions order from PROCESSING to SHIPPED. Logs ORDER_SHIPPED event with tracking number to Cassandra. Admin only.
Transitions order from SHIPPED to DELIVERED. Logs ORDER_DELIVERED event to Cassandra. Admin only.
Cancels an order. Any authenticated user. Logs ORDER_CANCELLED to Cassandra. Returns 422 if order is already SHIPPED or DELIVERED.
Expects HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity — order is already DELIVERED, cannot go back to CONFIRMED.

Transitions order DELIVERED → REFUNDED.

Kafka event published: OrderRefunded → shopverse.orders topic

Consumer handles:
  1. Publishes InventoryEvent.StockReleased → inventory topic (restores stock)
  2. Publishes NotificationEvent.PaymentSuccessNotification → notifications topic
     → RabbitMQ consumer sends refund confirmation email

Prerequisite: order must be in DELIVERED state (run steps ①–④ first).

item.name: 📦 Order Lifecycle (Kafka Events)
item.description:
These REST calls trigger domain events published to Kafka.

Flow:
  POST /api/orders           → OrderPlaced  → consumer: confirmation email + inventory reservation
  PATCH .../confirm          → OrderConfirmed → consumer: (logged, no email)
  PATCH .../ship             → OrderShipped  → consumer: shipping notification email
  PATCH .../deliver          → OrderDelivered → consumer: delivery notification email
  PATCH .../cancel           → OrderCancelled → consumer: stock released + cancellation email
  PATCH .../refund           → OrderRefunded  → consumer: stock released + refund email

DLT: messages that fail all 3 retries route to shopverse.orders.DLT
Retry: @RetryableTopic — 3 attempts, 1s/2s backoff (enabled by @EnableRetryTopic on main class)

request.description:
Places an order. Internally:
  1. Saves order to PostgreSQL (status: CONFIRMED — PlaceOrderUseCase calls confirm())
  2. Publishes OrderPlaced to shopverse.orders Kafka topic
  3. OrderKafkaConsumer receives it and:
     a. Sends OrderConfirmationNotification via RabbitMQ → confirmation email
     b. Publishes InventoryEvent.StockReserved to shopverse.inventory topic

Captures orderId automatically via test script.

CONFIRMED → PROCESSING path starts. Publishes OrderConfirmed.
Consumer: no email sent for this transition (confirmation already sent on OrderPlaced).

item.name: ③ Ship Order (publishes OrderShipped → shipping email)

request.description:
Publishes OrderShipped with trackingNumber.
Consumer: sends OrderShippedNotification via RabbitMQ → shipping confirmation email.

item.name: ④ Deliver Order (publishes OrderDelivered → delivery email)

request.description:
Publishes OrderDelivered.
Consumer: sends OrderDeliveredNotification via RabbitMQ → delivery confirmation email.

item.name: ⑤ Refund Order (publishes OrderRefunded → refund email + inventory)

request.description:
DELIVERED → REFUNDED. Publishes OrderRefunded.
Consumer:
  1. Publishes InventoryEvent.StockReleased (restores inventory)
  2. Sends PaymentSuccessNotification via RabbitMQ → refund confirmation email

Note: run steps ①–④ first so the order is in DELIVERED state.

item.name: ⑤-alt Cancel Order (publishes OrderCancelled → cancel email + inventory)

request.description:
Alternative to steps ③–⑤. Cancel from PENDING/CONFIRMED/PROCESSING.
Publishes OrderCancelled.
Consumer:
  1. Publishes InventoryEvent.StockReleased (restores stock)
  2. Sends OrderCancelledNotification via RabbitMQ → cancellation email

Use this instead of steps ②–⑤ if you want to test the cancellation path.
